result.target_topic: Investment structure and accounting method for tax credit VIEs
result.target_summary: The firm invests in nonconsolidated tax credit VIEs via limited partnership interests to receive income tax credits and benefits. As of January 1, 2024, the firm adopted ASU No. 2023-02, electing the proportional amortization method for qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects receiving production tax credits, with amortization and credits recorded in the provision for taxes.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
gs_2023_8_D316 details the firm's investments in qualified affordable housing projects using the proportional amortization method, including balances and amortization. gs_2024_8_D368 describes the adoption of ASU 2023-02 which expanded this method to include renewable energy projects, maintaining the proportional amortization accounting for these investments. Shared subject: Proportional Amortization Method for Tax Credit Investments.

Both disclosures describe the firm's investments in qualified affordable housing projects using the proportional amortization method. D316 (2023) provides the narrative description of funded investments, accrued commitments, and the amortization/credit recognition amounts ($301M amortization, $370M credits). D370 (2024) presents the tabular data for these same investments (amortization and tax credits/benefits). They cover the same specific subject matter: the financial details of proportional amortization investments.

comparisons.peer_topic: Tax Credit VIEs Asset Size and Structure
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the total assets of unconsolidated tax credit VIEs were $85.7 billion and $84.1 billion respectively, with unrelated third parties typically controlling significant activities.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC invest in unconsolidated tax credit VIEs structured as limited partnerships for affordable housing and renewable energy. However, the disclosures differ in focus: GS details its adoption of the proportional amortization method under ASU 2023-02 effective January 1, 2024, and how amortization is recorded in the provision for taxes. BAC focuses on the scale of these investments, reporting total assets of $85.7 billion as of December 31, 2024, and notes that unrelated third parties typically control the significant activities.

sentences.text: The firm makes equity investments in nonconsolidated tax credit VIEs that invest in qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects.

In connection with the adoption of ASU No. 2023-02, as of January 1, 2024, the firm elected the proportional amortization method for qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects that receive production tax credits.
The Corporation holds equity investments in unconsolidated limited partnerships and similar entities that construct, own and operate affordable housing, renewable energy and certain other projects.
The total assets of these unconsolidated tax credit VIEs were $85.7 billion and $84.1 billion as of December 31, 2024 and 2023.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of ASU No. 2023-02 for Tax Credit Structures
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi adopted ASU No. 2023-02 effective January 1, 2024, allowing the use of the proportional amortization method for certain tax-incentivized investments, which had no material impact on the financial statements.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi adopted ASU No. 2023-02 effective January 1, 2024, to use the proportional amortization method for eligible tax credit investments. GS explicitly states it elected this method for qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects, recording amortization in the provision for taxes. Citi also adopted the ASU but disclosed that it did not have a material impact on its financial statements, whereas GS's context implies active implementation with specific line-item impacts.

sentences.text: In connection with the adoption of ASU No. 2023-02, as of January 1, 2024, the firm elected the proportional amortization method for qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects that receive production tax credits.

The investments that meet the criteria for the proportional amortization method of accounting are amortized in proportion to the income tax credits and other income tax benefits received on such investments.
The ASU permits the Company to elect to use the proportional amortization method to account for an expanded range of eligible tax-incentivized investments if certain conditions are met.
Citi adopted the ASU on January 1, 2024, which did not have a material impact to the financial statements of the Company.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting change for tax-oriented investments to Proportional Amortization Method
comparisons.peer_summary: Effective January 1, 2024, the Firm adopted guidance to recognize amortization of certain alternative energy tax-oriented investments in income tax expense rather than other income, aligning with associated tax credits and benefits.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM adopted guidance in 2024 to recognize amortization of tax-oriented investments in income tax expense. GS states that amortization of investments meeting the proportional amortization method criteria is recorded as a component of the provision for taxes. JPM explicitly notes that as a result of adopting updates to the proportional amortization guidance, the amortization of alternative energy investments is now recognized in income tax expense, aligning with associated tax credits.

sentences.text: The investments that meet the criteria for the proportional amortization method of accounting are amortized in proportion to the income tax credits and other income tax benefits received on such investments.

The amortization of investments and the related income tax credits and other income tax benefits are recorded as a component of the provision for taxes, and are included in other operating activities in the consolidated statements of cash flows.

Proportional Amortization Method: Effective January 1, 2024, as a result of adopting updates to the Accounting for Investments in Tax Credit Structures Using the Proportional Amortization Method guidance, the amortization of certain of the Firm's alternative energy tax-oriented investments that was previously recognized in other income is now recognized in income tax expense, which aligns with the associated tax credits and other tax benefits.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of Proportional Amortization Method for Tax Equity Investments
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm adopted the accounting update for Investments - Equity Method and Joint Ventures - Tax Credit Structures on January 1, 2024, using the modified retrospective method, which permits electing the proportional amortization method for tax equity investments meeting certain conditions.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS adopted the accounting update for tax credit structures effective January 1, 2024, permitting the proportional amortization method. MS details the adoption via the modified retrospective method and notes that under this method, amortization is recognized net in the provision for income taxes. GS similarly adopted ASU No. 2023-02 and records the amortization of investments and related credits in the provision for taxes, though GS specifies the election applies to qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects.

sentences.text: In connection with the adoption of ASU No. 2023-02, as of January 1, 2024, the firm elected the proportional amortization method for qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects that receive production tax credits.

The investments that meet the criteria for the proportional amortization method of accounting are amortized in proportion to the income tax credits and other income tax benefits received on such investments.
The Firm adopted the Investments - Equity Method and Joint Ventures - Tax Credit Structures accounting update on January 1, 2024 using the modified retrospective method.

Under the proportional amortization method, the initial cost of the investment is amortized in proportion to the income tax credits and other income tax benefits received and recognized net in the income statement as a component of provision for income taxes.
